title: AI Fine-tuning and Derivative Works Restrictions — Exhibit (Template)
content:
Purpose and scope:

This Exhibit sets forth supplemental contractual terms governing the Vendor’s access to, use of, and retention of Customer Data and Model Outputs where such access may involve machine learning model inference, evaluation, or any activity that could lead to model training, fine-tuning, or creation of derivative models. The provisions below are intended to preserve Customer IP, prevent unauthorized model extraction or re-use, and establish practical audit and remediation procedures.

Definitions (capitalized terms used in this Exhibit):
- "Customer Data": any data, prompts, documents, files, or other inputs supplied by or on behalf of Customer to Vendor under the Master Agreement.
- "Model Outputs": any content, responses, embeddings, or artifacts produced by an ML model as a result of processing Customer Data.
- "Derivative Model": any model, weights, embeddings, or parameters that incorporate, were trained on, or were otherwise derived from Customer Data or Model Outputs.
- "Training": any process by which a model’s parameters are updated or adjusted using Customer Data, Model Outputs, or features computed therefrom, including batch fine-tuning, continual learning, prompt-tuning, embedding indexing that is used to change model behavior, or any method that results in persistent changes to model weights or representations.

1) Prohibition on Training and Derivative Works
1.1 Vendor shall not, under any circumstances, use Customer Data or Model Outputs to train, fine-tune, update, or improve any machine learning model (including Vendor-owned, third-party, or open-source models) without Customer’s prior express written consent. This prohibition applies to both direct and indirect training (including use via synthetic data produced from Customer Data).
1.2 Vendor shall not create, host, maintain, or distribute any Derivative Model that incorporates or is traceable to Customer Data or Model Outputs, nor shall Vendor permit any third party to do so.

2) Narrowly Permitted Uses (Audit, Safety Testing, and Performance Monitoring)
2.1 The following limited uses are permitted only if explicitly authorized in writing by Customer and subject to the technical and organizational controls set forth in Section 4:
  a) Non-persistent safety testing of Model Outputs to evaluate accuracy, toxicity, bias, or stability, where inputs and outputs are segregated, access-controlled, and instrumentation logs are ephemeral per Section 4.3.
  b) Aggregated telemetry on latency, error rates, and non-content metrics that do not include Customer Data or verbatim Model Outputs.
  c) Reproduction of specific failing examples for debugging when required to resolve an incident, provided that such examples are stored only for the duration necessary to remediate and are flagged for secure deletion thereafter.

3) Data Handling and Storage Controls
3.1 Segregation and Access Controls: Vendor must logically and physically segregate Customer Data and Model Outputs from other tenants. Access shall be granted on a least-privilege, role-based basis and only to personnel who require access to perform permitted activities. All access must be logged.
3.2 Ephemeral Processing Requirement: For any permitted testing described in Section 2.1(a), Vendor must process Customer Data and Model Outputs in ephemeral environments that do not persist data to long-term storage, and where all cache, logs, and intermediate artifacts are automatically purged within 72 hours unless Customer agrees to longer retention in writing.
3.3 Prohibition on Indexing for Behavioral Change: Vendor shall not index or otherwise materialize representations derived from Customer Data or Model Outputs (for example, creating searchable embeddings or feature stores) if such indexing could be used to change model behavior or produce persistent model artifacts.
3.4 Encryption: Customer Data and Model Outputs must be encrypted at rest using industry-standard cryptography (e.g., AES-256) and in transit (e.g., TLS 1.2+). Key management must allow Customer to assert key possession control where requested (BYOK/KMS integration options).

4) Logging, Telemetry, and Observability Constraints
4.1 Scope-limited Telemetry: Observability data sent to Vendor’s monitoring systems must not contain Customer Data or verbatim Model Outputs. Where traceability is required, pseudonymous identifiers are acceptable provided they cannot be reversed to reconstitute Customer inputs or outputs.
4.2 Audit Logs: Vendor must maintain immutable audit logs recording access to Customer Data and Model Outputs, including identity of accessor, timestamp, purpose, and duration. Logs relevant to security incidents must be retained for at least 12 months and made available for forensic review per Section 6.
4.3 Telemetry Boundaries: Any telemetry that incidentally contains small excerpts of outputs for debugging must be redacted or minimized by applying a profanity/personal data scrubber prior to storage, unless Customer authorizes retention for a defined remediation window.

5) Notice and Consent for Research or Internal Model Work
5.1 Any proposal by Vendor to use Customer Data or Model Outputs for internal research, model benchmarking, or vendor innovation must be submitted in writing to Customer, describing scope, technical controls, personnel, retention, and measures to prevent trailing influence on production models. Use is only permitted upon Customer’s prior written consent.

6) Audit, Attestation, and Evidence
6.1 Right to Audit: Customer or an agreed independent auditor may audit Vendor’s compliance with this Exhibit once per rolling 12-month period upon 30 days’ notice. Audits shall be limited to controls reasonably necessary to verify compliance (access controls, logs, ephemeral environment config, key management, and training prohibitions).
6.2 Attestation: Quarterly self-attestations shall be provided by Vendor’s security organization documenting adherence to the training prohibition and retention limits. The attestation shall include an executive summary of any exceptions and corrective actions taken.
6.3 Evidence Package: Upon request, Vendor will provide a redacted evidence package (logs, environment snapshots, KMS policies) supporting the attestation subject to reasonable non-disclosure terms.

7) Incident Response and Remediation
7.1 Notification: If Vendor becomes aware of any actual or suspected violation of Section 1 (including accidental use of Customer Data in a training dataset), Vendor must notify Customer within 72 hours, provide a root cause analysis within 14 days, and propose remedial actions including data purge, model retraining/rollback, and attestations of deletion.
7.2 Remediation Measures: Where Customer Data has been used in training or a Derivative Model has been produced, Vendor shall take reasonable steps to unwind the influence of that data (e.g., retrain affected models from clean checkpoints, remove artifacts, and certify deletion) and shall reimburse Customer for third-party forensic costs up to a capped amount if remediation is necessary.

8) Remedies and Equitable Relief
8.1 Injunctive Relief: The parties acknowledge that breach of the training prohibition would cause irreparable harm for which monetary damages are insufficient; Customer is therefore entitled to seek injunctive relief without posting bond.
8.2 Indemnity: Vendor shall indemnify Customer for direct losses arising from Vendor’s willful or negligent violation of this Exhibit, subject to limits in the underlying agreement but excluding speculative reputational harms unless expressly provided.

9) Termination and Transition Assistance
9.1 Termination Right: Customer may immediately suspend Vendor’s access to systems processing Customer Data upon reasonable belief of a material breach of this Exhibit.
9.2 Transition Assistance: Upon termination or expiration, Vendor will (a) provide a complete export of Customer Data and Model Outputs in a machine-readable format and (b) destroy all other copies and derivative artifacts relating to Customer Data or Model Outputs and provide a certified deletion attestation.

10) Carve-outs and Tailored Exceptions
10.1 Where Customer expressly permits narrow activities (for example, long-term retention for regulated archiving), the parties should document scope, personnel, retention periods, access controls, and compensating controls in a signed addendum. Any exception must be narrowly scoped and revocable in writing.

11) Definitions Revisited: Examples and Non-Exhaustive Illustrations
11.1 The following are examples to illustrate the Parties’ intent and are non-exhaustive:
  a) Prohibited: Vendor adds Customer support transcripts to a general-purpose training corpus used to update production model weights.
  b) Permitted with controls: Vendor runs a one-off safety test in an ephemeral sandbox to replicate a customer-reported hallucination and deletes sandbox artifacts after debugging.
  c) Prohibited: Vendor creates a searchable embedding index of Customer Data and uses that index as a retrieval-augmentation dataset for a production model.

12) Miscellaneous
12.1 Severability: If any provision is held unenforceable, the remainder shall remain in effect.
12.2 Governing Law and Venue: Same as the Master Agreement unless otherwise specified.
12.3 Integration: This Exhibit supplements the Master Agreement and in the event of conflict the stricter data protection obligation governs.

Annex A — Minimal evidence checklist for audits (non-exhaustive):
- Logical separation diagrams and tenant configuration screenshots
- Access control lists and RBAC role definitions for last 12 months
- Sample ephemeral environment teardown scripts and retention configs
- KMS policies and proof of BYOK integrations (if used)
- Sample audit log extracts (redacted) showing access, purpose, and deletion events
- Quarterly self-attestations and any remediation reports

Annex B — Suggested contract language (short form insert for SOWs/POs):
The Vendor shall not use Customer Data or Model Outputs to train, fine-tune or otherwise improve any machine learning models or create derivative models, except as expressly and separately authorized in writing by Customer. Any permitted testing shall use ephemeral environments with automatic purge within 72 hours unless Customer agrees otherwise in writing.

Notes to reviewers (internal):
- Consider whether 72-hour ephemeral retention is acceptable for compliance customers; some regulated sectors may require shorter windows or on-prem-only testing.
- Liaise with SRE on how ephemeral environments will be instantiated and audited (IAAS snapshots, ephemeral K8s namespaces, HSM/BYOK).
- Add a capped remediation cost schedule to Section 7.2 aligned to procurement thresholds for template adoption.
